nodes.label: CI Pipeline (Biome lint, typecheck, Turbo build)
CSS Design Tokens (dark/light)
nodes.author: Garib
nodes.rationale: No hardcoded colors allowed outside the token file; every token has a value in both themes so the theme switch is lossless.

nodes.label: Volt & Ember Brand Palette
nodes.author: Garib
nodes.rationale: Only two accent colors by design to protect brand identity. Volt (#D4F233) is legible on black but disappears on white, so light mode swaps it to a sports green (#5A8A00) that keeps WCAG AA >= 4.5:1 contrast.

nodes.label: Dark-First Dual Theme
nodes.author: Garib
nodes.rationale: Dark theme is the canonical design because the product is used outdoors on phones (referees, organizers); light is a faithful adaptation, not a degraded version.

nodes.label: Bebas Neue / DM Sans Typography Scale
nodes.author: Garib
nodes.rationale: Bebas Neue reserved for high-impact numbers (scores, stats); DM Sans in weights 300/400/500 only — 600/700 read too heavy in this system.

nodes.label: Perfil Puente (Guest Player)
nodes.rationale: Removes adoption barrier: captains register players by name only (is_guest = true) so leagues work before every player has an account.

nodes.label: Identity Linking Rule (never auto-merge)
nodes.rationale: The platform never infers or merges identities by name similarity — linking always requires two-step human confirmation to avoid corrupting player history.

nodes.label: Protected Tournament Lifecycle (created_under_plan)
nodes.rationale: A tournament started under a paid plan never degrades when the subscription lapses: feature flags evaluate current plan OR created_under_plan, whichever is greater. Protects competition integrity and works as retention.

nodes.label: forces_game_ejection Sanction Flag
nodes.rationale: Abstracts multi-sport ejections (red card, 5 fouls, umpire ejection) under one technical flag so the sanctions engine is sport-agnostic.

nodes.label: Motor de Elegibilidad
nodes.rationale: Eligibility is validated against the real account (user_id), never the guest profile; suspensions are scoped per tournament, never platform-global.

nodes.label: Walkover Resolution
nodes.rationale: Walkover score always comes from tournaments.settings.walkover_score, never hardcoded, so each league keeps its own rulebook.

nodes.label: referee_session_token Access
nodes.rationale: Referees record match events via a tokenized link without needing an account; access is strictly limited to the assigned match. Captains and coaches are explicitly excluded from event capture.

nodes.label: Hybrid Roles & Permissions Model
nodes.rationale: Preconfigured roles with DB-scoped limits; permissions are backend validations per resource, never just UI restrictions. Multitenant: one user, different roles per organization.

nodes.label: Subscription Plans (Free/Starter/Pro/Elite)
nodes.rationale: Plans billed per organization, not per user, so organizers are not penalized for growing their community.

nodes.label: No-Intermediary Payment Model
nodes.rationale: 4Sports never holds tournament money: Captain -> Gateway -> Organizer, 0% commission. Revenue is SaaS subscription only, avoiding financial-intermediary legal exposure.

nodes.label: Tournament Lifecycle States
nodes.rationale: draft -> private/open_registration -> active -> completed -> archived; structure freezes at publish, incidents remain editable with audit + public notification.

nodes.label: orgGuard(minRole)
nodes.rationale: Role hierarchy viewer(0) < organizer(1) < admin(2) < owner(3); verifies active Redis context matches :orgId and membership is active.

nodes.label: Git Workflow (pre-push rebase + lockfile sync)
nodes.rationale: pnpm-lock.yaml is regenerated on every install; rebasing onto development and reinstalling before push prevents unresolvable lockfile merge conflicts.

nodes.label: Match Lifecycle State Machine
nodes.rationale: Strict state machine on matches.status (scheduled/postponed/live/suspended/finished/disputed/walkover/cancelled) — states cannot be skipped, preserving competition integrity.

nodes.label: Match Finish Atomic Transaction
nodes.rationale: POST /matches/:id/finish runs score calc, winner, standings recalc, suspension confirmation, BullMQ enqueue and bracket advance in ONE PostgreSQL transaction — full rollback on any failure so a match never ends inconsistent.

nodes.label: Full Standings Recalculation (no incremental deltas)
nodes.rationale: Recalculation reads ALL finished matches and rebuilds the table from scratch instead of applying deltas, to avoid drift/inconsistencies after corrections and disputes.

nodes.label: Live Match WebSocket Protocol (ws://api/ws/matches/:id)
nodes.rationale: Sub-5-second score latency target; Redis caches active match state to shield PostgreSQL during simultaneous write peaks — DB stays the source of truth.

nodes.label: Layered API Architecture (routes -> use-case -> repository)
nodes.rationale: Layers never mix: routes only call use cases, use cases only call repositories, repositories only run Drizzle queries; Redis is handled by the use case, never routes or repositories.

nodes.label: R2 Presigned Upload Flow (POST /v1/upload/presigned)
nodes.rationale: Clients never upload files through the API; the API only issues a 5-minute presigned PUT URL and later stores the public URL — keeps upload bandwidth off the API.

nodes.label: Project Context & Stack Decisions
nodes.rationale: Bun over Node for performance/native TS; ElysiaJS for Bun-native TS inference and WebSockets; Drizzle over Prisma for SQL-first edge compatibility; JSONB in Postgres instead of MongoDB; R2 for zero egress fees; Railway for zero-ops deploys.

nodes.label: Multitenant Context Switching (UC-005)
nodes.rationale: Active context lives in Redis session, never localStorage; every backend request validates membership status and resource scope, returning 403 outside scope.

nodes.label: Groups -> Playoffs Transition (UC-106)
nodes.rationale: Transition is always manually triggered by the organizer (with overrule drag-and-drop) — never automatic — so administrative decisions like disqualifications can be applied before the bracket freezes.

nodes.label: On-the-fly Standings Calculation (UC-108)
nodes.rationale: Rank is never stored fixed; every query recomputes from completed matches applying settings.tiebreaker[] hierarchically. Tiebreakers lock after the first completed match.

nodes.label: Team Ownership Model (is_owner / is_player)
nodes.rationale: Ownership and roster presence are dimensions independent of the visible role: is_owner (exactly 1 per team, enforced by partial unique index) grants exclusive privileges; is_player controls roster/convocatoria inclusion. Lets a coach own the team without appearing in lineups.

nodes.label: Player Transfer Flows (UC-210 free / UC-211 three-signature)
nodes.rationale: Off-season transfers are free; in-tournament regulated transfers require three signatures (staff, player, organizer) inside a configurable window. Past stats stay frozen with the old team.

nodes.label: .expo Local Folder
nodes.rationale: The .expo folder is machine-specific (recent devices, dev server settings) and must not be committed; it is auto-added to .gitignore on project creation.

nodes.label: BetterAuth Session Cookie Authentication (Client Side)
nodes.rationale: Web relies on browser cookie handling via fetch credentials:'include'; mobile must persist and resend the better-auth.session_token cookie manually (expo-secure-store or BetterAuth RN client) because React Native has no cookie jar.

nodes.label: NativeWind v4 + Tailwind v3 Styling Stack
nodes.rationale: Mobile deliberately pins NativeWind v4 with Tailwind v3 because the NativeWind + Tailwind v4 combination is not yet stable for production.

nodes.label: Primary Color Tokens (tailwind.config.js)
nodes.rationale: Design tokens (primary-50..primary-900, sky-blue scale) are centralized in apps/mobile/tailwind.config.js theme.extend so new colors are added in one place.

nodes.label: @4sports/ui Shared Component Package
nodes.rationale: Components in packages/ui affect web and mobile simultaneously, so the team rule is: check for an existing component before creating one, and coordinate (Ivan asks Garib) before adding new shared components.

nodes.label: Expo Router v4 File-Based Navigation
nodes.rationale: Expo Router was chosen for its file-system routing that mirrors Next.js App Router, keeping the mental model identical across web and mobile: each .tsx under app/ is a route, (auth) groups omit URL segments, [id].tsx is a dynamic route.

nodes.label: authGuard Middleware
nodes.rationale: Every private route must apply authGuard as an Elysia plugin before the handler; it lives at src/shared/middleware/auth.guard.ts.

nodes.label: orgGuard(minRole) Middleware
nodes.rationale: Routes operating on an organization apply orgGuard with a minimum role (e.g. orgGuard('organizer')); lives at src/shared/middleware/org.guard.ts.

nodes.label: featureGuard(feature) Middleware
nodes.rationale: Routes gated behind a subscription plan apply featureGuard('feature_key'); lives at src/shared/middleware/feature.guard.ts.

nodes.label: Thin Route Handler Rule
nodes.rationale: Route handlers in routes.ts may only call a use case and pass the result to toApiResponse; business logic never lives in HTTP handlers so it stays testable and transport-agnostic.

nodes.label: Use Case Result Pattern
nodes.rationale: Business logic is a pure async function (repo, input) -> Promise<Result<T>> that never throws; it returns ok(data) or err(domainError) so error flow is explicit and type-checked under strict TypeScript (no any, no ! assertions).

nodes.label: BetterAuth OpenAPI Reference (/auth/reference)
nodes.rationale: BetterAuth self-generates OpenAPI docs for all /auth/* routes via the openAPI() plugin registered in src/shared/lib/auth.ts, so auth endpoints never need hand-written docs.

nodes.label: _sandbox/note Reference Module Template
nodes.rationale: The _sandbox/note module is the complete reference implementation of the domain module layout (entity, repository, drizzle repository, errors, use-cases, http/v1) and is the mandated template for new modules.

nodes.label: Docker Compose Dev Services Index
nodes.rationale: Each dev service ships as a standalone compose file with a named volume for persistence, so services can be started and stopped independently.

nodes.label: Log Pipeline (API file -> Promtail -> Loki -> Grafana)
nodes.rationale: The API is fully decoupled from observability: it only writes JSON log lines to a file, and Promtail/Loki/Grafana are optional Docker containers layered on top, so the app has zero runtime dependency on the log stack.

nodes.label: LOG_FILE Environment Variable
nodes.rationale: LOG_FILE=logs/api.log makes Pino tee JSON logs to a file (relative to apps/api/) in addition to pretty terminal output, for Promtail to scrape. It must NOT be set in production, where writing JSON to stdout only is the correct behaviour for hosted environments.

nodes.label: Promtail Service (4sports-promtail)
nodes.rationale: Mounts ../../apps/api/logs read-only into /logs/api so log scraping needs no Docker socket and no agent inside the API process.

nodes.label: Grafana Service (4sports-grafana, host port 3001)
nodes.rationale: Anonymous access is enabled with Admin org role (GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_*) so local developers query logs without login; host port 3001 avoids clashing with the web app on 3000.

nodes.label: Grafana Loki Datasource Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Provisioned as the default datasource (isDefault: true) pointing at http://loki:3100 so Grafana is query-ready on first boot with no manual setup.

nodes.label: Loki Single-Node Config (tsdb + filesystem)
nodes.rationale: Dev-only single-node setup: auth disabled, in-memory ring, replication_factor 1, tsdb schema v13 on local filesystem, samples older than 168h rejected, analytics reporting off.

nodes.label: Promtail api_logs Scrape Config
nodes.rationale: Tails /logs/api/*.log with static label service=api and promotes JSON fields level and type to Loki labels so LogQL can filter on them.

nodes.label: Pino Numeric Level to String Mapping
nodes.rationale: Pino serializes log levels as numbers (10..60) when transport.targets is used (a Pino limitation), so a Promtail template stage maps 10->trace .. 60->fatal to keep the Loki level label human-queryable ({level="error"}).

nodes.label: pnpm Workspace Definition (apps/*, packages/*)
nodes.rationale: Workspaces span apps/* and packages/*; build scripts are explicitly allowlisted (esbuild, msgpackr-extract, sharp) under allowBuilds instead of allowing arbitrary postinstall scripts.
